title: "3. Maps"
description: "Ready-made maps in one line: static maps for papers and interactive maps to explore."
ordem: 3
tempo: "10 min"
---

Maps need three packages, installed once:

```r
install.packages(c("sf", "ggplot2", "leaflet"))
```

## Static map

```r
library(localdatasus)

circ <- obitos_bairro("Rio de Janeiro", 2023, cid = "I")
mapa_bairro(circ, titulo = "Deaths from circulatory diseases, Rio de Janeiro, 2023")
```

![](../../imagens/mapa-circulatorio-rio.png)

- **Color:** by default, the map is colored by the **rate per 10,000 inhabitants**.
- **Boundaries:** official IBGE neighborhood boundaries (2022 Census), downloaded once per state.
- **Grey:** neighborhoods without data.

### Choose what to color and the palette

```r
mapa_bairro(circ, valor = "obitos")             # color by the count ("valor" = value)
mapa_bairro(circ, cores = "Blues")              # other palettes: "YlOrRd", "Greens", "Purples"...
```

### Automatic panels

If the table has a `por` breakdown (or several years), the map is split into panels:

```r
por_sexo <- obitos_bairro("Rio de Janeiro", 2023, cid = "I", por = "sexo")
mapa_bairro(subset(por_sexo, sexo != "Ignorado"))
```

![](../../imagens/mapa-sexo-rio.png)

### Other places

::: {layout-ncol=2}
![Deaths by district, São Paulo, 2023](../../imagens/mapa-distritos-sp.png)

![Dengue by neighborhood, Joinville, 2024](../../imagens/mapa-dengue-joinville.png)
:::

```r
mapa_bairro(obitos_bairro("São Paulo", 2023), cores = "Blues")
mapa_bairro(agravos_bairro("dengue", "Joinville", 2024))
```

### Customize and save

`mapa_bairro()` returns a regular **ggplot2** plot:

```r
library(ggplot2)
mapa <- mapa_bairro(circ) + labs(subtitle = "Source: Rio de Janeiro City Health Department")
ggsave("map.png", mapa, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 300)
```

## Interactive map

```r
mapa_interativo(agravos_bairro("dengue", "Rio de Janeiro", 2024))
```

The map opens in RStudio's *Viewer*, over a street basemap. Hover over a neighborhood to see its name, or click it to see cases, rate and population. To save it as a web page:

```r
m <- mapa_interativo(circ)
htmlwidgets::saveWidget(m, "map.html")
```

## In QGIS

Every table has `lat` and `lon`. In QGIS, use *Layer → Add Layer → Delimited Text*, with X = `lon` and Y = `lat`. For polygons, join on `codigo_ibge` with the IBGE neighborhood boundaries.
